entities.summary:
Matteo Orsini was an Italian Dominican friar and Cardinal, born in unknown year, died on August 26, 1340. He played a pivotal role in the Catholic Church during the Middle Ages, serving as a diplomat and advisor to Pope Clement VI. Orsini's influence extended beyond his administrative duties, shaping the theological debates of his time through his involvement with the Dominican Order.

As a member of the College of Cardinals, Orsini participated in several key papal conclaves, including that which elected Pope John XXII. His connections to powerful figures like Pope Clement VI and King Louis I of Hungary demonstrate the far-reaching nature of his influence.

Orsini's legacy is also evident in the numerous theological treatises he penned, including works on the nature of the Trinity and the sacraments. These writings not only showcased his intellectual prowess but also contributed to the development of Dominican theology.

In conclusion, Matteo Orsini's significance lies in his multifaceted role as a diplomat, theologian, and administrator within the Catholic Church. His contributions to the Church's hierarchy and theological debates make him an important figure in the annals of medieval history.
